core_obligations: Choose a quasi-isomorphism F^• → I^• into a K-injective complex; the product complex H'^• represents R SheafHom(E^•,F^•) by the internal-hom construction, so it suffices to show H^• → H'^• is a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 11799-11806).

For every open U: H^0(H^•(U)) = Hom_{K(O_U)}(E^•|_U, I^•|_U) → H^0(H'^•(U)) = Hom_{D(O_U)}(E^•|_U, I^•|_U); by the local-actual lemma the sheafifications of U ↦ H^0(H^•(U)) and U ↦ H^0(H'^•(U)) agree (proof lines 11807-11825).
A similar (shifted) argument for the other cohomology sheaves concludes the quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 11826-11829).
proof_roadmap: Fix a K-injective resolution and identify the representing complex.
Compare on opens and identify sheafifications with the local-actual lemma.
Handle the remaining degrees by the same argument.
difficulty_reason: Compare the hom complex H^• with the product complex H'^• computing the internal hom against a K-injective resolution; on opens, H^0 of the hom complex computes homotopy classes, and the local-actual lemma identifies the sheafifications; the remaining degrees follow by the same shifted argument.
